scope: local browser, existing shared services and authorized SQLCipher database

automated_tests.data: fabricated fixtures, temporary databases, test encryption keys and simulated responses only
covered: six registered metrics across both supported windows agree with shared analysis and reproduce
latest pending, unscorable and calibrating records do not fall back to older valid values
missing fields and dates remain null; same-day activities remain individual observations
cycle and workout strain remain separate
measurement, metric update, interval update, capture and knowledge timestamps remain distinct
source revisions, late responses, deletion, expiry and cleanup during a view
loopback peer, exact Host, Origin and Fetch Metadata boundaries
HttpOnly SameSite session, sync CSRF, bounded JSON and static file whitelist
sanitized unexpected errors without raw exception propagation to server logging
thread-owned connections, concurrent sync deduplication, failure and durable resume
real-mode HTTP reads use a test SQLCipher database without a plaintext copy
demo and invalid real launches reject before protected store access

tooling.chart_js_license_and_source_integrity: passed; MIT and fixed package/file hashes included

live_checks.final_server_parallel_dashboard_and_stat: passed; connected and idle after sync
live_checks.health_data_handling: all records, numeric checks and credentials remain local; only technical check statuses returned
live_checks.browser_preview_handoff: requested for the same loopback URL; app returned queued

not_run: browser interaction automation, DOM inspection, screenshots and visual or responsive acceptance
complete history, daily coverage and field-by-field reconciliation
outside_scope: health data sent to models, real MCP or WebMCP
webhooks, scheduled synchronization, notifications and coaching
limitations: A 30-day requested window does not establish that every date contains data.
Displayed values remain in local browser memory until the page is refreshed or closed.
Loopback, same-origin and session checks are not independent authentication between local OS users or programs.
HTTP and syntax verification do not establish browser visual or interaction acceptance.
